Introduction

The sporadic variety of Stiffman syndrome (SS) is a central nervous system (CNS) disease characterized by continuous/fluctuating muscular rigidity and painful spasms.

She failed to respond to carbamazepine and intravenous phenytoin, but responded dramatically to high-dose diazepam and baclofen. During her second hospital stay, the child developed mild rhabdomyolysis after a cardiorespiratory arrest. Valproate and steroids added to her treatment regimen led to sustained improvement. During 4-year follow-up in the outpatient department, the child's spasms have resolved, although mild stiffness of the lower leg/abdominal/chest/girdle muscles with restriction of neck movements have persisted and the stiffness increases with exercise or sleep deprivation. She is fully ambulant and attends normal school.
